cases.title: Digital arrest: FD broken, then a transfer during a long video call
cases.why_expected: A first payment far above anything she has ever sent (₹287 usual), to an account in a flagged mule network, 3 hours after breaking an FD, during a 95-minute internet call from an unknown number. Every family should agree.

cases.title: Digital arrest: retiree sends ₹1.5 lakh by RTGS to a brand-new account
cases.why_expected: ₹1.5 lakh to an account opened weeks ago, after an FD break, during a 140-minute internet call from an unknown number. He has a trusted contact, so a trusted check or hold is the right response.

cases.title: Fake trading app: third, larger 'top-up' after a fake profit
cases.why_expected: A rising series of payments to new accounts, a small credit from a stranger, and now 44× his usual payment to a mule-network account. No call, but journey and payee should agree on their own.

cases.title: Task scam: 'like YouTube videos' job asks for a bigger prepaid task
cases.why_expected: Two small credits from strangers followed by a rising series to new accounts (₹2k → ₹4k → ₹6k), the last to a newly opened account. The amounts are small, but the shape is the textbook task-scam ladder.

cases.title: Fake customer care: screen shared and remote app open during a refund call
cases.why_expected: Screen sharing and a remote-access app during a call from an unknown number, paying 32× her usual amount to a new account. Screen sharing during a payment is close to a scam by itself.

cases.title: Marketplace 'scan to receive': buyer's QR takes money instead
cases.why_expected: A first payment of 4× his usual to a newly opened account during a short call from an unknown number. The amount is modest, so we may only reach a pause; even a pause would save him here.

cases.title: Cloned voice of a grandson asking for bail money
cases.why_expected: First payment, 23× the customer's usual, during an 8-minute phone call from an unknown number. The payee looks clean (no flag yet), so only journey and context can carry this; a pause or trusted check is right, a hold may not be reachable without an outside flag.

cases.title: Fake instant-loan app: fourth 'processing fee'
cases.why_expected: A rising series of fees to new accounts, and the payee is already reported on the cybercrime portal. An outside flag plus the series should be enough to stop it.

cases.title: Digital arrest (Hindi): payee's number rated high fraud risk
cases.why_expected: ₹60,000 (45× usual) to a first-time payee whose linked number DoT rates high fraud risk, during a 75-minute internet call from an unknown number. Hindi screen should carry the same warning.

cases.title: Fake trading: trader's largest 'deposit' after weeks of fake gains
cases.why_expected: For a trader ₹75,000 is only 7× usual, but it follows a rising series to new accounts and a stranger credit, and the payee is in a live mule network.

cases.title: Security deposit to a new landlord
cases.why_expected: 62× his usual payment to a first-time payee, so a pause is defensible. But nothing is flagged on the payee and there is no call: holding the money would be wrong.

cases.title: Hospital bill paid while on the phone with the billing desk
cases.why_expected: A 60+ customer paying 60× usual to a new payee during a call from an unknown number looks like a scam, so a pause or trusted check is acceptable. The payee is clean, so it must never be held.

cases.title: Buying a second-hand bike from a seller he met
cases.why_expected: 11× usual to a new individual: a pause is understandable. The caller is a saved contact and the payee is clean, so no hold.

cases.title: First fee to a new home tutor
cases.why_expected: Close to her usual payment (₹3,894), clean payee, no call. Nothing here should slow her down.

cases.title: Wedding caterer advance by IMPS
cases.why_expected: ₹1.2 lakh to a first-time payee is 11× his usual, so a pause is acceptable for a sum this large. Nothing else is wrong; no hold.

cases.title: Trader pays a new supplier
cases.why_expected: About 2× his usual and a third of what he moves on a normal day. New suppliers are routine for him.

cases.title: Money to her son while talking to him
cases.why_expected: 10× her usual, but to a saved contact she pays often, and the caller is in her contacts. At most a note.

cases.title: Grocery payment at a shop
cases.why_expected: A merchant payment: these skip scoring entirely and should never be interrupted.

cases.title: Monthly payment to the regular vendor
cases.why_expected: A regular vendor, about his usual payment size. Nothing new.

cases.title: Sending money to a cousin's long-unused account
cases.why_expected: A dormant account waking up to receive 15× his usual looks like a mule pattern, so a pause is fair. No flag on the payee and no call: never a hold.

cases.title: Splitting: fourth ₹9,500 transfer in two hours to a clean-looking mule
cases.why_expected: Each part is only 2.4× her usual and the payee is unflagged, but four payments to four new accounts in two hours is a series. We may miss it if the series features don't push the journey family high enough.

cases.title: Chat-only investment coaching, no call, clean payee
cases.why_expected: Rising series and a stranger credit, but no call and an unflagged payee. Only the journey family sees it; we expect at best a pause and no hold, and may miss it entirely.

cases.title: Digital arrest with consent off: no phone signals at all
cases.why_expected: Without consent the context family cannot vote, so the call is invisible. Journey (FD break, 296× usual, new payee) and payee (mule network) should still agree. Context is sent here to check it is dropped.

cases.title: Marketplace scam: the first tiny test payment
cases.why_expected: Below her usual payment, only a short call. We expect to miss this (a known Round 1 failure case): the amount is too ordinary to cross the pause line.

cases.title: Loan-fee scam: the very first ₹999 fee, no call
cases.why_expected: A single small fee to a new account with nothing else unusual. We expect to miss it; the series that would give it away has not started yet.

cases.title: Digital arrest paid into a dormant account
cases.why_expected: No outside flag on a dormant account, so no hold is possible. Journey and a 50-minute unknown internet call should give at least a pause or trusted check; we may miss it if the dormant account looks ordinary.

cases.title: Genuine payment to a new payee during a long call from an unknown number
cases.why_expected: This looks just like a digital arrest (60+, 23× usual, long unknown call). A pause or trusted check is acceptable; the payee is clean, so a hold would be a false alarm we must not make.

cases.title: 60+ customer buys gold from a new jeweller
cases.why_expected: 72× his usual to a new payee looks alarming, so a pause is fair, but there's no call and no flag: never a hold.

cases.title: Fake customer care on a customer who has not opted in
cases.why_expected: Screen sharing and the call are invisible without consent. 7× usual to a newly opened account may be enough for a pause; we may miss it because the payee family alone may not cross its line.

cases.title: Investment scam's first deposit to a clean-looking account
cases.why_expected: 4× usual, one stranger credit, no call, clean payee. We expect to miss it: the series hasn't started and nothing outside points at the payee yet.
